- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when true values rise sharply after a dip.
- Overestimates peak prices following recent spikes, then fails to correct downward quickly — overshoots persist for 2–3 days.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual market momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after sharp rises, then undercorrects upward after sharp falls — exhibits oscillatory error patterns.
- Forecasts show higher variance than actual price paths, especially in the final 5–10 days — model overfits short-term noise.
- When true price rises above 75, model often fails to adjust upward sufficiently — underestimates tail risk in high-price regimes.
- In low-price regimes (below 70), model tends to underestimate further, creating a “floor effect” — fails to recognize sustained support levels.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent history (last 5–7 days) is underweighted in forecasts, leading to lagged responses to new data.
